title: Transparent boundary conditions for the spatially discrete Schrödinger equation: Reflectionless quantum transport in 1D lattices
authors: Mashrab E. Akramov, Jambul R. Yusupov, Matthias Ehrhardt, Davron U. Matrasulov
abstract: We construct exact transparent boundary conditions (TBCs) for a time-continuous, spatially discrete Schrödinger equation that models a one-dimensional quantum lattice. Using a recently developed exact solution for the discrete system, we derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps analytically via Laplace transforms. This yields a convolution-type boundary condition governed by Bessel functions. We rigorously demonstrate the consistency of this discrete formulation with its continuous counterpart in the continuum limit. Additionally, we present an efficient time-discretization scheme based on the trapezoidal rule for practical implementation. Numerical experiments using a Crank-Nicolson solver verify that our proposed TBCs eliminate spurious backscattering entirely and preserve reflectionless propagation of a Gaussian wave packet exiting the computational domain
summary: This paper constructs exact transparent boundary conditions (TBCs) for the spatially discrete Schrödinger equation modeling 1D quantum lattices. By utilizing Laplace transforms and solving the characteristic equation, the authors derive a convolution-type TBC that ensures reflectionless quantum transport. The method is validated numerically to show perfect wave packet exit without spurious backscattering.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop mathematically exact transparent boundary conditions (TBCs) for simulating quantum wave propagation on finite, discrete lattices.
main_result: The derived TBCs successfully eliminate spurious backscattering and preserve reflectionless transport of a Gaussian wave packet exiting the computational domain in numerical tests.
method: The authors derive the TBC by analytically solving the spatially discrete Schrödinger equation using Laplace transforms and matching boundary conditions (Dirichlet-to-Neumann map).
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional quantum lattice governed by the time-continuous, spatially discrete Schrödinger equation. The method rigorously checks consistency with its continuous counterpart in the continuum limit.
key_observables: The decay of the discrete norm M(t) over time, which should monotonically decrease to zero as the wave packet exits the domain.
important_parameters: The lattice spacing parameter (h), and the boundary index J defining the finite computational domain.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on using an exact analytical solution for the discrete Schrödinger equation, providing a mathematical advantage over methods that approximate continuous boundaries.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows complex plane trajectories confirming the physical admissibility of the derived root $\xi_+(s)$. Figure 2 and 3 show numerical verification of stable propagation and monotonic decay of the wave packet norm, respectively.
paper_structure: The paper follows a theoretical derivation path: first establishing the problem setup via the discrete Schrödinger equation; then applying Laplace transforms to derive the TBC in the frequency domain; subsequently performing inverse Laplace transforms using Bessel functions to obtain the time-domain condition; finally, implementing and testing this condition numerically with standard solvers.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly rigorous and mathematically exact framework for absorbing boundaries in discrete quantum systems, which is crucial for simulating open quantum systems or wave propagation in engineered lattices without artificial reflections.
